name: VA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by about 22 points, among the reddest on the ballot
Griffith holds a roughly 8-to-1 fundraising edge with $879,000 on hand
Prediction markets price the race at about 97 percent Republican
No public polls or expert ratings; national environment tilts modestly toward Democrats
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Griffith's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and markets pricing the race at 97 percent Republican leave Joy Powers little apparent path, even with an environment that favors Democrats by several points nationally.
model.watch: A large national Democratic wave paired with late outside spending could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat would require a shift far beyond anything currently signaled.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Virginia's 9th District sits in the state's far southwest and leans Republican by about twenty-two points, among the most Republican districts on the ballot this year. Morgan Griffith has held the seat since 2011 and is running again after winning renomination. His Democratic challenger, Joy Powers, enters the general election with modest resources.

Fundraising shows a wide gap: Griffith has raised about $2.2 million with $879,000 on hand, while Powers has raised roughly $257,000 with $60,000 available, and outside groups have spent little on either side. Prediction markets give Griffith roughly a 97 percent chance of winning. No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the outlook rests on the district's strong Republican lean, Griffith's incumbency, and his money advantage, all pointing to a safe Republican hold despite a national environment that tilts somewhat toward Democrats.
